bootstrap.what: test AUC(best DKT) - AUC(best BKT), resampling test students

conclusion: DKT now ranks first on the Synaptic simulator, but only narrowly: its best variant (“best A + time features on input + upcoming attempt”) reaches test AUC 0.7356 against 0.7285 for the best BKT (“Per-skill BKT (EM)”), a gain of +0.0071 (95% bootstrap interval over test learners +0.0032 to +0.0109) with log-loss 0.5964 vs 0.5985. That is below the +0.02 AUC the app's gate (src/lib/dkt/compare.ts) requires, so the gate's answer is still “don't switch”. The evidence: the untuned Lab 3 DKT lost (0.7062) mainly because it was under-trained — early stopping with a higher learning rate alone lifted it to 0.7287 (validation 0.7277, level with BKT's 0.7285). Time features, the suspected cause, helped but only a little (0.7356, +0.0055 on validation), because the simulator's learners forget slowly over 60 days and most of the remaining error is elsewhere: on first attempts at a skill (2,801 test answers) BKT scores 0.504 and DKT 0.493; on repeats after a day or more (10,925) 0.638 vs 0.651. DKT+ regularisation did not help (best 0.7276 validation). More data is the lever that matters: per-skill BKT stays flat while DKT keeps improving, so the gap goes +0.0071 at 1,000, +0.0192 at 3,000, +0.0196 at 5,000 learners, flattening between 3,000 and 5,000 and still just short of +0.02 at 5,000. Both models remain far below the simulator's own ground-truth ceiling (0.8438), which knows each learner's hidden memory state; that gap, not BKT vs DKT, is where the headroom is.

next_steps.step: Collect real shadow-log data, and plenty of it, before deciding anything
next_steps.evidence: Every number here is from simulated learners whose memory model was written by hand, and the ranking flips between datasets (DKT +0.09 on ASSISTments 2009, −0.02 untuned here). Phase D shows DKT's lead grows with volume while BKT's does not, so the decision should be taken on a large real log (the app's gate already demands ≥ 5,000 attempts).

next_steps.step: Per-learner memory parameters (learner ability, per-learner decay) in either model
next_steps.evidence: The ground-truth ceiling (0.844) sits ~0.1 AUC above every model; the simulator draws per-learner learn, stability, slip and guess, which neither per-skill BKT nor DKT's input represents directly.

next_steps.step: Richer time modelling: exponential per-skill decay with learnable rates (DKT-forget / HLR-style), not log-gap features
next_steps.evidence: Log-gap time features were the single biggest gain after training fixes (+0.0055 validation AUC).

next_steps.step: Attention model (SAKT/AKT) as a second deep baseline, once there is more data
next_steps.evidence: At 1,000 learners capacity was not the bottleneck (hidden 200 was no better than 50 on validation); larger models were not re-tuned at 3,000-5,000 learners.

next_steps.step: Drop DKT+ regularisation and BKT forgetting-per-attempt from further work
next_steps.evidence: Phase C (DKT+) did not beat plain early-stopped DKT on validation, and BKT with p_forget matched plain BKT at every data size: forgetting in the simulator is driven by elapsed days, which a per-attempt forget rate cannot see.

app_export.note: No app-format export: the best DKT variant does not beat tuned BKT by ≥ 0.02 test AUC, so the condition for exporting it to the app's synaptic-dkt.json format is not met. The app is unchanged.
